methodology: To decompose the original research topic and the generated technical specification into atomic units, I systematically analyzed both texts to identify distinct requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was defined as an independent and self-contained statement that is technically specific and unambiguous. I focused on extracting key functionalities, input/output specifications, and operational behaviors that could be implemented as individual requirements. This approach ensured that all critical aspects of the design were captured in a structured manner.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The flip-flops can selectively modify their output based on byte-enable inputs.
The byte-enable inputs control writing to the upper byte (d[15:8]) or lower byte (d[7:0]) of the 16-bit register.
The resetn signal is a synchronous, active-low reset.
All D flip-flops are triggered by the positive edge of clk.
The output q is a 16-bit register reflecting the written data.
spec_atomic_units: The module implements a 16-bit register file with 16 D flip-flops.
The clk input triggers the D flip-flops on the rising edge.
The resetn signal is active-low, resetting outputs to 0 on the next rising edge of clk.
The byteena[1] and byteena[0] signals determine which bytes of input data are written.
The output q is updated based on the state of resetn and byteena signals.
The design includes timing logic ensuring setup and hold times are met for the D flip-flops.
